solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: American barmen’s price bleed funds sadly (6,9)

indicatorNotes.sadly: done sadly, the letters are in a poor state, knocked out of order

blocks.note: the fifteen letters of PRICE BLEED FUNDS, rearranged
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A complaint that American bar staff are charging so much it drains your money.
annotation.walkthrough: "Barmen" suggests people pulling pints; here they are members of the bar, lawyers. The 's stands for "has", joining definition to wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Public defenders are the lawyers a US court appoints for people who cannot pay, so they are American members of the bar.

entries.clue: Factory in Bury (5)

blocks.note: a works where goods are manufactured
the verb: to put something in the ground, as a gardener does with bulbs

annotation.surface: A factory located in Bury, a town near Manchester.
annotation.walkthrough: Bury is a Lancashire mill town, so a factory in Bury is a natural picture; the capital letter hides the verb meaning to put in the ground.
annotation.definitionFit: Plant means an industrial works, and to plant is to set something in the earth, which is burying it.

entries.clue: Man with money finally appropriated cloth rep’s patch (9)

indicatorNotes.finally appropriated: the final letter is taken away, appropriated, from the word before

blocks.note: a bishop is a chessman
RICH, having money, with its final letter taken

annotation.surface: A wealthy man grabbing a patch of cloth from a salesman.
annotation.walkthrough: "The cloth" means the clergy, so a cloth rep is a churchman, and his patch is the area he looks after. "Man" is a chess piece.
annotation.definitionFit: A bishopric is a diocese, the territory a bishop, a senior representative of the clergy, is responsible for.

entries.clue: Island connected with Columba ultimately? (4)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimately means at the end, so it takes the final letter of Columba

blocks.note: I is the standard abbreviation for island
on can mean connected with, as in on the phone
last letter of Columba

annotation.surface: Asking which island is linked to Saint Columba.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: Saint Columba founded a monastery on Iona, a small island off the west coast of Scotland, in 563.
annotation.definitionFit: Iona is the island forever tied to Columba, who brought Christianity to Scotland from there.

entries.clue: Nit-pick about light that overlooks river (7)

indicatorNotes.about: about means turned around, so the word is written backwards
indicatorNotes.that overlooks: in a down answer, something that overlooks another sits on top of it, so it comes first

blocks.note: an LED, a light-emitting diode, is a small light
the Ouse is a river in England, a crossword regular

annotation.surface: Someone being pedantic about a lamp with a river view.
annotation.walkthrough: "Nit-pick" reads as quibbling; taken literally it means picking nits, the eggs of lice, out of hair.
annotation.definitionFit: To delouse is to rid someone of lice and their nits, which is picking nits in the literal sense.

entries.clue: Agitated tirade bores female in charge (7)

indicatorNotes.bores: to bore is to drill into something, so the tirade goes inside

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female
a rant is a tirade
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

annotation.surface: A woman in charge is worked up and her angry speech tires everyone.
annotation.walkthrough: "Bores" wants to mean wearies the listeners; it is drilling, one piece pushed into the middle of another.
annotation.definitionFit: Frantic means wildly agitated, as with fear or worry.

entries.clue: Con artist confused one on horse, perhaps (9)

blocks.note: the nine letters of CON ARTIST, rearranged
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A swindler muddled about someone riding a horse.
annotation.walkthrough: "Horse" is slang for heroin, so a person on horse is a drug user, not a rider; "perhaps" marks heroin as one example of a narcotic.
annotation.definitionFit: A narcotist is someone who takes narcotics, and heroin is one.

entries.clue: Choice between drugs is not half trivial (5)

indicatorNotes.between: the second piece sits between the two drugs
indicatorNotes.not half: only half of the word is kept

blocks.note: E is ecstasy, and plural drugs gives it twice
LITTLE, trivial, cut to its first half

annotation.surface: Picking between two drugs is said to be no small matter.
annotation.walkthrough: "Not half" in British speech means very much; here it is literal, keeping only half of LITTLE.
annotation.definitionFit: Choice as an adjective means the best, and the elite are the best of a group; used as an adjective, elite means the same.

entries.clue: Some hangers-on or antsy heads of Women’s Institute? (9)

indicatorNotes.Some: some of the letters, so the answer is part of the phrase that follows

blocks.note: hangerS-ON OR ANTSy

annotation.surface: Some restless followers of the Women's Institute leadership.
annotation.walkthrough: The Women's Institute is a British women's organisation, often shortened to WI; its "heads" are its first letters, W and I, and both are sonorants in phonetics.
annotation.definitionFit: Sonorants are speech sounds made with a free, unobstructed flow of air, and the sounds of W and I both qualify; the question mark flags this example.

entries.clue: Tracks by artist reviewed in a magazine (7)

indicatorNotes.reviewed: reviewed read as re-viewed, looked at again from the other end

blocks.note: lanes are tracks
RA, Royal Academician, the standard crossword artist

annotation.surface: An artist's music tracks getting a review in a magazine.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a music magazine reviewing an album; the magazine is the kind that holds weapons.
annotation.definitionFit: A magazine is a store for arms and ammunition, which is exactly what an arsenal is.

entries.clue: Find fault with a shower escaping from trap (7)

indicatorNotes.escaping from trap: trap is slang for mouth, so words escaping from it are spoken

blocks.note: a rain is a shower

annotation.surface: Complaining that water is leaking out of a trap.
annotation.walkthrough: "Trap" looks like a snare; it is slang for mouth, as in "shut your trap".
annotation.definitionFit: To arraign is to accuse, and in older use to find fault with or censure.

entries.clue: God’s flipping rubbish, hospitaller at front admitted (4)

indicatorNotes.flipping: flipped over, the word reads backwards
indicatorNotes.admitted: the letter is let into the word

blocks.note: ROT, rubbish, turned round
first letter of hospitaller

annotation.surface: An outburst calling a knight hospitaller's god a load of rubbish.
annotation.walkthrough: "Flipping" reads as a mild British swear word, like "flipping heck"; here it turns ROT round. The 's is short for "is".
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Norse pantheon's hammer-wielding thunderer is one god among many.

entries.clue: I push a lot as fighting always overwhelms you (10)

indicatorNotes.overwhelms: to overwhelm is to engulf, so the letters go around the word for you

blocks.note: action is fighting, as in killed in action
e'er, the poetic contraction of ever
U sounds like you, the text-speak spelling

annotation.surface: A pushy fighter explaining they shove a great deal because combat always gets the better of them.
annotation.walkthrough: "A lot" reads as a great deal; it is an item for sale at auction, which the speaker pushes to bidders.
annotation.definitionFit: An auctioneer's job is to sell lot after lot, pushing each one to the highest bidder.

entries.clue: Heavenly wrath bearing ridicule and enmity primarily (3,4)

indicatorNotes.primarily: primarily means first, so take the first letter

blocks.note: someone's air is their bearing or manner
to rag is to tease or ridicule
first letter of enmity

annotation.surface: Divine anger that brings with it mockery and hostility.
annotation.walkthrough: "Heavenly wrath" suggests an angry god; the heavens here are just the sky, where the passengers fly.
annotation.definitionFit: Air rage is violent anger by passengers on a plane, fury up in the skies.

entries.clue: Substance that stops a relief worker crossing river (9)

indicatorNotes.crossing: the parts cross the river, so it sits in among them

blocks.note: the word a, kept as it stands
R is the abbreviation for river
rest is relief from work
the worker ant, the standard crossword worker

annotation.surface: A substance that stops an aid worker as they ford a river.
annotation.walkthrough: "Relief worker" reads as one aid worker; it splits into two pieces, relief and worker.
annotation.definitionFit: An arrestant is a substance that halts a process, such as bleeding or a chemical reaction.

entries.clue: Macaroni cheese at last cooked for refreshment (9)

indicatorNotes.cooked: cooked ingredients are altered and mixed, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, taken as printed
last letter of cheese
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Macaroni cheese has finally been cooked and is ready to eat.
annotation.walkthrough: "Macaroni cheese" is a single dish in the surface; only the E of cheese is used, and the answer is a drink, not food.
annotation.definitionFit: An Americano is espresso diluted with hot water, a coffee to refresh you.

entries.clue: Tory housing limits can make you colour (7)

indicatorNotes.housing: to house something is to hold it inside

blocks.note: Con is short for Conservative, and a Tory is a Conservative
rims are edges, limits

annotation.surface: The limits a Tory government puts on housing could make you go red with anger.
annotation.walkthrough: "Tory housing" reads as Conservative housing policy; "housing" is the container instruction. Tories are the UK's Conservative Party.
annotation.definitionFit: Crimson is a deep red colour, and to crimson is also to go red.

entries.clue: We see Song dancing round American wingers (4,5)

indicatorNotes.dancing round: letters that dance around each other change places

blocks.note: the nine letters of WE SEE SONG, rearranged
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Watching a performer called Song dance around some American wide players.
annotation.walkthrough: "Wingers" reads as wide players in football or rugby; here it means birds, creatures with wings.
annotation.definitionFit: Snow geese are white geese that breed in the Arctic and winter across North America.

entries.clue: Noises of fiddles? (7)

blocks.note: a racket is a loud noise
a fiddle is a swindle, and so is a racket

annotation.surface: The sounds that violins make.
annotation.walkthrough: "Fiddles" reads as violins; it is British slang for dishonest schemes, and the question mark flags the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: Racket means both a din and a fraudulent scheme.

entries.clue: Southern acts featuring piano icons (7)

indicatorNotes.featuring: the acts feature the piano, holding it within them

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
p is piano, softly, in music
rites are ceremonial acts

annotation.surface: Musical acts from the South who are legends of the piano.
annotation.walkthrough: "Icons" suggests legends; it means small computer images, and "acts" means ceremonies, not performers.
annotation.definitionFit: In computing a sprite is a small image moved around a screen, much like an icon.

entries.clue: Drinks lots, but not when rector is around (7)

indicatorNotes.not when rector is around: the word is used, but not with the R for rector in it

blocks.note: portions are lots, shares
R is the abbreviation for rector; it is taken out

annotation.surface: Someone drinks heavily, except when the parish priest is nearby.
annotation.walkthrough: "Drinks lots" reads as a heavy drinker; the split falls between the two words, and "lots" is the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Potions are drinks, especially medicinal or magic ones.

entries.clue: Pressure related to petty row worthy of religion (7)

blocks.note: P is the symbol for pressure
on means about, related to, as in a book on birds
a tiff is a minor quarrel

annotation.surface: Pressure from a trivial argument over something religious.
annotation.walkthrough: "Worthy" is a noun here, an important person, not an adjective meaning deserving.
annotation.definitionFit: The Pontiff is the Pope, the most eminent figure in the Catholic Church.

entries.clue: Religion’s mad about daughter being a man (10)

indicatorNotes.mad about: mad letters are in disorder, and about signals turning them round

blocks.note: anagram fodder, including the S
D is the abbreviation for daughter
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Someone's religion is fanatical about a daughter becoming a man.
annotation.walkthrough: "Man" is a soldier, as in officers and men, so being a man is serving in the ranks; the surface points to gender instead.
annotation.definitionFit: Soldiering is serving as a soldier, and in military speech the men are the rank-and-file soldiers.

entries.clue: Let love’s first blush relieve you of worry (5)

indicatorNotes.first blush: at first blush means at first sight, so take the first letter

blocks.note: first letter of love
to ease someone is to relieve their worry

annotation.surface: A plea to let the first flush of romance calm your fears.
annotation.walkthrough: "Let" looks like the start of a request; it is the definition, to rent out.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from property talk: renting a flat out to a tenant can be called either.

entries.clue: A Republican hoarding endless petroleum jelly (4)

indicatorNotes.hoarding: to hoard is to keep something stored inside
indicatorNotes.endless: the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: the word a, as printed
GAS, the American word for petroleum fuel, without its last letter
R is the abbreviation for Republican

annotation.surface: A Republican stockpiling petroleum jelly with no end in sight.
annotation.walkthrough: "Petroleum jelly" reads as one thing, Vaseline; it splits, with "jelly" the definition. Gas is the American term for petrol.
annotation.definitionFit: Agar is a jelly made from seaweed, used in cooking and in laboratories.

entries.clue: Contrary knight and earl regularly in The Sun? (5)

indicatorNotes.Contrary: contrary means going the opposite way, so the word is written backwards
indicatorNotes.regularly: take letters at regular intervals, every other one

blocks.note: SIR, a knight's title, turned round
the first and third letters of EARL

annotation.surface: A tabloid story about a difficult knight and an earl in The Sun newspaper.
annotation.walkthrough: "The Sun" looks like the British tabloid; it is the star, which rises every morning, and the question mark admits it is one example.
annotation.definitionFit: The sun rises every day, so it is a riser, one that gets up.

entries.clue: Drink noisily mostly and sound like you’re 27? (4)

indicatorNotes.mostly: most of the word, all but the last letter

blocks.note: SLURP, drink noisily, without its last letter

annotation.surface: Gulping a drink loudly and ending up sounding drunk.
annotation.walkthrough: 27 across is THE WORSE FOR WEAR, meaning drunk, and drunk people slur their words.
annotation.definitionFit: To slur is to run words together indistinctly, as a drunk person does.

entries.clue: Legendary rock and pop singer from the Eighties? (7)

blocks.note: a stone of myth, said to be too hard to break
a British new-wave star of the early 1980s, famous for his warpaint stripe

annotation.surface: A music-press tribute to a legendary rock and pop star of the 1980s.
annotation.walkthrough: "Legendary rock" reads as rock music of legend; it is a stone from legend. Adam Ant was a British chart star of the 1980s.
annotation.definitionFit: Adamant was the name for a legendary rock too hard to break, and the letters also spell Adam Ant.

entries.clue: One given lines by head for disorder (7)

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
L is line, doubled for the plural
a ness is a headland, as in Orford Ness on the Suffolk coast

annotation.surface: A pupil given lines by the head teacher as punishment for bad behaviour.
annotation.walkthrough: In British schools "lines" is a punishment of copying out a sentence many times; "the head" is the headteacher. Here head is a headland, and disorder is a medical one.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the medical sense, where a disorder is a condition of ill health rather than a mess.

entries.clue: Where fate and sorrow mix to make you happy (3,5,3,4)

blocks.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder, joined by "and"
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A philosophical line about joy coming from the mixing of fate and grief.
annotation.walkthrough: "Happy" reads as cheerful; in British slang it means merry, tipsy, which is how someone the worse for wear is.
annotation.definitionFit: To be the worse for wear is to be drunk, and happy is a mild word for the same state.
